record.original_question: Prove that the positive imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are not all rational multiples of one another.

evidence.quote: Problem 2: Prove that the positive ordinates of ζ(s) are not all rational multiples of one another.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\zeta(s)$ denote the Riemann zeta function, defined for $\operatorname{Re}(s)>1$ by $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{-s}$ and extended to a meromorphic function on $\mathbb{C}$ with a simple pole at $s=1$. A nontrivial zero of $\zeta(s)$ is a zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ lying in the critical strip $0<\operatorname{Re}(s)<1$. Let $\{\gamma_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ denote the (multi)set of positive imaginary parts (ordinates) of the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$, listed with multiplicity.

Prove that the ordinates $\{\gamma_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ are not all pairwise rational multiples of one another; equivalently, show that there exist indices $m,n$ such that $\gamma_m/\gamma_n \notin \mathbb{Q}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The full Linear Independence Conjecture (that the positive ordinates of nontrivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$) remains an open conjecture in analytic number theory, going back to Wintner. The weaker statement that they are not all rational multiples of one another also appears to be open: recent work (e.g., effective formulations of LIC by Martin and others, 2023–2024) still treats this as conjectural, with no unconditional proof known.

status_evidence.title: An effective Linear Independence Conjecture for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function and applications
status_evidence.snippet: The Linear Independence Conjecture (LIC), which asserts that the ordinates γ are linearly independent over Q, has deep implications... It remains an open conjecture in analytic number theory.
status_evidence.claim: Linear independence over Q of the ordinates remains an open conjecture, which implies the weaker statement that not all are rational multiples of each other.

status_evidence.title: Riemann zeta function - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Linear Independence Conjecture concerns the imaginary parts of the zeros of the zeta function.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference identifies the linear independence of zeta ordinates as a conjecture.
